body.p: Remarks

As stated above, Applicant appreciates the Examiner's thorough examination of the subject application and requests reexamination and reconsideration of the subject application in view of the preceding amendments and the following remarks.

As of the subject action, claims 1-6, 8-16, and 19-30 were pending in the subject application, of which claims 1, 19, and 27 are independent claims. With this Response, Applicant has amended claims 1, 19, and 27. Applicant respectfully submits that no new matter is believed to have been entered as a result of this Response. All objections and rejections are respectfully traversed.

Claims 1-6, 8-16, and 19-30 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for lack of antecedent basis for "the second vision subsystem". Without conceding the rejection, Applicant has removed "the second vision subsystem" from the claims. Accordingly, claims 1-6, 8-16, and 19-30 are believed to be in condition for allowance. As such, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection be withdrawn.

Claims 1-6, 12-16, 19-23, and 27-30 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being anticipated by Morey et al. (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2021/0031361, hereinafter referred to as "Morey") in view of Edinger et al. (U.S. Patent No. 9,346,160, hereinafter referred to as "Edinger"). Claims 8-11 and 24-26 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Morey in view of Edinger, and further in view of Gilbertson et al. (U.S. Patent No. 9,827,678, hereinafter referred to as "Gilbertson"). Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Without conceding the rejection and in an effort to accelerate prosecution of the subject application, Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 19, and 27. Representative independent claim 1 is recited below for convenience:
1. (Currently Amended) A detachable, self-contained robotic arm
system comprising:
a mounting subsystem configured to releasably engage an
operating platform, wherein the operating platform is an autonomous
mobile base;

a slew ring coupled to the mounting subsystem; a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem using the slew ring, wherein the robotic arm subsystem is directly coupled to the slew ring, wherein the slew ring pivots the robotic arm subsystem relative
to the mounting subsystem;

a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled directly to the slew ring, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to pivot with the robotic arm subsystem during motion of the robotic arm subsystem and to enable visually monitoring of
areas proximate the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system;

a control subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem and configured to effectuate movement of the robotic arm assembly using the first machine vision subsystem and the second machine vision subsystem;
and
a connectivity subsystem configured to detachably couple the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system to one or more external
systems.
Support for these amendments may be found in at least FIGS. 1-2 and paragraph [0037]
of the subject application as filed, which are reproduced below for convenience.
SVG {EMBED HERE} 3.493.733 .
[0037] A slew ring is shown which serves as joint A for the arm. This provides a pivoting motion for the base of the arm relative to the robot and the control box.

Note that in this embodiment the motor powering the slew ring is placed above and along the main axis of the electronics control box and mounting bracket attached to the slew ring base which allows the vertical observation post, to pivot with the motion of the arm. This allows continuous observation of the arm and
payload and to avoid collision of the moving arm with the observation post.
(See, subject application, FIGS. 1-2 and paragraph [0037]).

Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of Morey, Edinger, and/or Gilbertson fails to teach, disclose, or even suggest "a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem using the slew ring, wherein the robotic arm subsystem is directly coupled to the slew ring, wherein the slew ring pivots the robotic arm subsystem relative to the mounting subsystem"; and "a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled directly to the slew ring, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to pivot with the robotic arm subsystem during motion of the robotic arm subsystem and to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system."

For example, in rejecting independent claim 1, the subject action states "Morey teaches a robotic arm system comprising: a robotic arm subsystem (206) mounted on a platform (top surface of 202) which is an autonomous mobile base (202); a slew ring (804 at 602) between the robotic arm subsystem and the mobile base for pivoting the robotic arm subsystem with respect to the mobile base; a first machine vision subsystem (214) mounted on a mast assembly (210) coupled (indirectly) to the slew ring, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to pivot with the robotic arm subsystem (section [0088] describes a serial connection such that rotation of midsection 204 causes any structure located above 204 to also rotate) during motion of the robotic arm subsystem and to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the robotic arm system; and a control subsystem (inherent, such as 118) configured to effectuate movement of the robotic arm assembly using the first machine vision subsystem." See, subject action, p. 3. Paragraph [0088] and FIGS. 3 and 8B of Morey are reproduced below for convenience.

[0088] Notably, the spine and actuator architecture illustrated in FIG. 7 allows different coaxial portions of a robot to rotate independently of one another about their respective rotational axes. This architecture may be contrasted with an alternative structure where stacked components are serially connected together

such that, upon rotation of midsection 204 or a portion thereof (e.g., rotational joint for arm 206 that forms part of midsection 204), any structures located above midsection 204 are also rotated. That is, such alternative structure does not include a structural component, such as spine 500, which extends through
multiple coaxial portions of the robot.
(See, Morey, paragraph [0088] and FIGS. 3 and 8B).

As can be seen from at least the above-cited portions of Morey, the combination of Morey, Edinger, and/or Gilbertson is not understood to teach, disclose, or suggest a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem using the slew ring, where the robotic arm subsystem is directly coupled to the slew ring; and a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled directly to the slew ring. As such, Applicants respectfully submit that the combination of Morey and Edinger is not understood to teach, disclose, or suggest Applicant's claimed "a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem using the slew ring, wherein the robotic arm subsystem is directly coupled to the slew ring, wherein the slew ring pivots the robotic arm subsystem relative to the mounting subsystem"; and "a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled directly to the slew ring, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to pivot with the robotic arm subsystem during motion of the robotic arm subsystem and to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system."

Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-6, 8-16, and 19-30 under § 103 as being unpatentable over the combination of Morey, Edinger, and/or Gilbertson be withdrawn.

In this response, Applicant has amended various claims and/or asserted arguments in this application to facilitate expeditious prosecution of the application. Applicant is not conceding that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to the instant action, and/or having interpretations other than presented herein are unpatentable over the art cited by the Examiner. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue claims in one or more continuing applications, including claims capturing the subject matter encompassed by any claims prior to this response, claims having different interpretations than presented in this response, and additional claims.

In consideration of the amendments and foregoing discussion, Applicant respectfully asserts that the subject application is in condition for allowance. While Applicant respectfully asserts that the subject application is now in condition for allowance, the Examiner is invited to telephone Applicant's representative (617-854-1420) to facilitate prosecution of this application. Please apply any charges or credits to the above-noted deposit account.
Respectfully submitted,
